content_sections.body: In bus ticket, put finished actions in a clear order. Use time words such as yesterday, first, then, and this morning. Example: “I needed a ticket to the airport.” The past action tells the listener what happened; the time word tells when.
content_sections.title: Notice the language

content_sections.body: I needed a ticket to the airport. The clerk told me the price and departure time. Ask: what detail would a friend need next? Say the key action once, then add one time or place detail.
content_sections.title: Context and meaning

content_sections.body: Choose a true or invented bus ticket detail. Say two connected sentences: one about what happened and one about the next step. Check that the order is easy to follow.

speaking.instruction: Roleplay: you are a customer or friend dealing with bus ticket; the tutor is the staff member or friend who has one missing detail. Scenario: explain what happened and ask for the next step. Tutor opening: “Hi, what happened?” Ask one follow-up about time, place, quantity, or result; finish when the tutor understands and you agree on the next step.
